correctness.rationale: Walsh nonnegativity is \(Q(s)=1+\sum_{i<j}a_{ij}s_is_j\ge0\). Averaging over balanced signs for even \(d\), or the sign-sum-one slice for odd \(d\), gives the sharp objective bounds, and the radial choices attain them. Equality forces \(Q\) to vanish on the relevant slice. In odd dimension, sign swaps plus spanning of the slice force all edge coefficients equal. In even dimension, balanced-slice row differences force the additive form \(a_{ij}=u_i+u_j\); then \(Q(s)=(\sum s_i)(\sum u_is_i)\), and positivity is exactly the stated subset family. A fresh exact replay verified the radial inequalities and odd equality-slice full rank through dimension eight; the frozen verifier extends exact checks through dimension ten and gives explicit nonradial even examples.

final_claim: For positive-definite functions on \(\mathbb F_2^d\) supported at Hamming weights zero and two and normalized by \(f(0)=1\), the Turán constant is \(d\) for even \(d\) and \(d+1\) for odd \(d\). Odd \(d\) has the unique radial extremizer \(a_{ij}=2/(d-1)\); for even \(d\), all extremizers are exactly \(a_{ij}=u_i+u_j\) with \(\sum_i u_i=1\) and \(\sum_{i\in B}u_i\le1/2\) for every \(|B|<d/2\).
